FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Watch for large trucks and underpowered cars losing speed on steep grades or taking longer to accelerate into traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles commonly travel at 25 mph or less. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
The handbook says these slow vehicles should carry an orange triangular slow-moving-vehicle emblem at the rear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Reduce speed in crowded places where maneuvering room is limited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
Shopping areas, parking lots and downtown streets can require lower speeds because vehicles and pedestrians move unpredictably in several directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Rush-hour congestion and hurried drivers are reasons to consider slowing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
Narrow bridges and tunnels may require slower travel because opposing vehicles pass closer together. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
At toll plazas, watch for lane changes, stops and acceleration, and for the lane count changing on either side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, remain ready for children entering the roadway without looking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
At railroad crossings, check for trains and space beyond the tracks, slow for rough crossings and avoid blocking the tracks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
Nighttime reduces how far and how readily a driver can detect objects, and familiar surroundings can appear different. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
Approaching-headlight glare can impair vision while the eyes readjust to lower light. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
Avoid outdriving the headlights by choosing a speed that permits stopping within the visible roadway ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
When meeting vehicles at night, use brief glances to judge their lane position rather than staring into their headlights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A01
At night, use quick checks to maintain your position and identify the road’s right edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A01
Continue looking ahead for objects in the vehicle’s path while managing nighttime glare. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A02
Do not assume a flashing turn signal guarantees a turn; plan for the other driver either turning or continuing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
Do not assume every driver will obey a stop sign or red signal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
Continually consider an escape route and note the shoulder and surrounding area before an emergency occurs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
If an opposing vehicle begins passing without apparent room, slow down and be prepared to use a previously identified escape route if necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0126]
